html:
SMTO-BOOT-0045 — SMTO is missing a part it needs to start

GUID: fc1cdeb9-e1c8-49f0-ae4e-d1c85685df76
Slug: startup-dependency-missing
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: startup

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because part of the program, or a file it was told to use, couldn't be found.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details on this screen to see the name of what's missing. It tells you whether a part of the program or one specific file is missing.
  2. If you start SMTO from its project folder with ./startup.sh, run ./install.sh in that folder, then start SMTO again. If you use the installed app, reinstall the same version. Missing program parts usually come from an incomplete install or update, and the installer puts them back.
  3. If SMTO is started with a settings file (the --config option), make sure that file still exists in the same place. SMTO stops if a settings file it was told to use has been moved or deleted.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and your conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder to fix this; it holds your conversations.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Startup failed because a required Python module could not be imported or a required installed resource or explicitly configured file was not found (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError or FileNotFoundError).

What this means

  • Startup could not import a required module or open an installed resource. The failed stage identifies the component being initialized. Source installations need the matching environment and dependencies; packaged installations need the complete matching artifact. Preserve runtime data while repairing the installation.

Why this can happen

  • Startup could not import a required module or open an installed resource. The failed stage identifies the component being initialized. Source installations need the matching environment and dependencies; packaged installations need the complete matching artifact. Preserve runtime data while repairing the installation.

How to diagnose it

  • A required Python module could not be imported during startup.
  • The previously failing startup stage completes in the intended environment.

How to fix it

  • Read Technical details or the Server terminal for the missing module or path. For a source checkout, rerun ./install.sh with the same Python and start with ./startup.sh; for a packaged install, reinstall the matching version. If the missing file is an explicit --config or AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH file, restore it or remove the reference; keep the data directory intact.
  • Restore the matching SMTO installation and required dependencies for this platform. Start with the supplied launcher and interpreter, then restart the service.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition and run the diagnostic again. Rechecking does not replay tasks or completed operations.

How to verify the fix

  • The previously failing startup stage completes in the intended environment.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
